pricing: Free forever (ad-free logging, own plans, all videos, CSV); Pro $12.99/mo or $79.99/yr US with 14-day trial on yearly - paywalls plan/workout generator, progression recommendations, charts, multiple gyms, RIR/periodization/deloads, plate & warm-up calculators, exercise evaluations, custom exercise images.
platforms: iOS (iPhone), Android; no Apple Watch/Wear OS app, no web logger
positioning: Hypertrophy/strength logger with a program generator and per-set weight/rep recommendations constrained by the gym's real available weights.

features.how: 8 metric types per exercise: weight+reps, counterweight(assistance)+reps, reps only, reps+duration, duration only, distance+duration, weight+distance, weight+duration. Each set also shows a computed performance metric (e1RM, e10RM or volume, per setting).

Working sets, dropsets (app calculates drop weight from last working set; generator can add them), supersets, and warm-up sets from the Pro warm-up calculator - warm-ups aren't logged as sets but can be copied into notes with one tap. No documented failure/AMRAP set type.

RIR (not RPE) is a Pro feature, toggled per plan or workout; half values allowed (e.g. 1.5). Once enabled, RIR must be entered for every set. Plans can carry RIR targets that recommendations aim for; without tracking the algorithm infers RIR.

Previous sets and notes stay visible in the logger. 'Reference workout' setting (Settings > Training): 'Same plan day' (default; previous performance of that exercise on the same plan day, fallback to most recent) or 'Last workout' (most recent regardless of plan).
Editable weight/reps fields are pre-filled with values from the reference workout; Pro recommendation shown separately as a blue bubble under the same set.

Any number of notes per exercise in a workout. Two kinds: temporary workout notes (shown later as previous-workout info) and pinned exercise notes (shown every time, editable on exercise page); toggle by (un)pinning. Notes aren't included when sharing plans.
Supersets supported in plans and workouts (also usable to shorten sessions); generator output editable to add supersets. No circuits/giant-set terminology documented.
features.user_feedback: Older review: can't modify supersets mid-workout (thefitnesstribe, undated/older).

features.how: Long-press an exercise thumbnail in the workout header and drag; plan editor allows moving exercises between days (v6.4, Jan 2026) and importing workouts/days from other plans.

Replace shows a list of similar exercises (e.g., different equipment when machine is taken) or normal search/filters; targets kept where possible (v6.5). At workout end, prompt asks whether to apply changes to the plan or keep them only for today.
Pro: built into the weight picker for bar-and-plate exercises (uses bar weight + plate inventory of active gym); if target can't be built shows next lower achievable weight.

Pro: tailored warm-up sets before working sets scaled by exercise, first working set weight, target reps, available weights and experience. Configurable count per compound/medium/isolation and per cold/warm muscle, extra/fewer sets for very low/high reps, and % of working weight per warm-up set (e.g., 35%, 65%).

Each built-in bodyweight exercise stores the % of bodyweight moved (custom exercises: user sets 0-100%). User logs only added weight or assistance (e.g., -15 kg on assisted dips); bodyweight is included in e1RM/e10RM and recommendations. Resistance bands available as equipment.
No per-side tracking documented; exercise 'Misc' instructions say whether to log one dumbbell or both.
No tempo field documented.
Free: create a standalone workout from scratch; Pro can generate a standalone workout.
Past workouts can be opened, edited or deleted; changes propagate to stats. Past workouts can be added manually (suggested in lieu of import).
Custom 'Picker' for weight/reps/RIR shows a sorted list of likely values plus keyboard ('Weight, reps and RIR in two taps'); horizontal thumbnail tab bar to switch exercises.
features.user_feedback: Older review: text entry lag in exercise search (thefitnesstribe).

features.how: Starts automatically on set completion; alarm at zero; by default counts past zero to show actual rest. Rest timer is in the free tier.
Defaults per exercise type (e.g., longer for large compounds, shorter for isolation) plus per-exercise override; current rest can be adjusted without changing the default.
'Rest timer with alarm'; live countdown in iOS Live Activity / Android live notification. Whether a push alert fires when backgrounded isn't explicitly documented.
features.user_feedback: Review lists 'No audio cues' as a con (fitnessdrum 2026).

features.how: iOS Live Activity (since v6.6, Apr 2026; iOS 16+): exercise/set counts, current exercise, set and recommendation; during rest the whole activity becomes a countdown bar; Dynamic Island shows rest timer and one-tap return. Android live notification equivalent (can be disabled).
Duration-based metric types exist (duration only, reps+duration, weight+duration, distance+duration) for planks, burpees, runs; dedicated in-set stopwatch/countdown UI not documented.
Generator shows an estimated workout duration (incl. warm-ups, rest, transitions); whether the in-workout elapsed timer exists is not documented.
An 'active workout reminder' notification exists (v7.0 fixed it firing after a completed workout); resume of workouts referenced. Auto-finish behaviour not documented.

Free: unlimited manual plans (multi-day) and standalone workouts. Plan editor with bulk editing across all exercises, a day, or a week of a periodized plan; edit sets, rep targets, dropsets; import days from other plans.
No folders documented.

Multi-week plans: generated plans 4-7 weeks (default 4) or indefinite; manual plans 1-52 weeks or indefinite; repeat/extend/regenerate at the end. No curated library of named programs - entry points are generate, build own, or open a shared plan link.

Pro: periodization across a mesocycle (plans >=2 weeks) varies sets, rep targets, dropsets and RIR targets week to week; optional deload at plan end (not for indefinite plans) or mark any workout as deload. Not %1RM-based.
features.user_feedback: Advanced users praise built-in periodization replacing Excel (App Store reviews).

features.how: Pro, server-side (needs internet). Inputs: gender, experience (Beginner <6 mo, Intermediate 6+ mo, Advanced 1.5+ y, Pro 4+ y, Elite 8+ y), gym equipment, goal (Max strength / Muscle gain / Strength endurance -> rep targets), frequency, relative duration, muscle priorities (prioritize/deprioritize, relative), split (Automatic incl. hybrids, Full body, Upper-lower, Push-pull, PPL, PPL-upper-lower), plan length, optional RIR/periodization/deload. Outputs split, exercises, order, sets, reps, dropsets; some randomness among equal options. Standalone workout generator: Full body/Upper/Lower with nested focus (e.g., Upper > Push > Chest) or auto-focus from recent training.
Plans are a sequence, not calendar-bound: missed workouts just continue with the next; only a weekly workout target (1-7) for streaks.
Free: share plans or workouts via unique link and QR code; includes name, exercises (also custom), targets, supersets - no logged sets or notes. Recipient gets an editable copy.
795 built-in exercises (Sept 2026), curated for strength/hypertrophy, plus home, stability and cardio exercises.

Every exercise has a real video filmed in a gym by certified trainers (no stock/animations), sometimes multi-angle; text sections Setup, Execution, Misc (cues, mistakes, how to count weight). Offline videos in lower resolution.

Create or copy an existing exercise: name, image (Pro, from camera/library), equipment, main muscle, multiple auxiliary muscles, type (compound/isolation...), metrics, bodyweight involvement 0-100%. Not used by generators.
Main targeted muscle + auxiliary muscles per exercise; muscle filter; charts for sets per muscle.
Database shows only exercises available with the active gym's equipment (custom always shown); per-exercise whitelist/blacklist overrides.

Search plus filters (muscle, equipment, type: large compound/medium/small isolation/stability/cardio) and sorts: Most used, Most recent (shows time since last), Most popular (default; based on 25M workouts), A-Z; shows count performed.
Exercise content in 13 app languages (EN, DE, ES, FR, PT-BR, IT, PL, TR, NL, SV, NO, DA, JA).
Pro: rates each exercise's suitability for muscle building based on range of motion and stability.

Pro, per working set: estimates achievable performance via an internal estimated 10RM from reference workout + today's completed sets, then picks a weight (hard constraint: available weights in active gym) and reps close to plan target, weighting deviations; optional RIR target. Updates set to set within a workout, can go down after underperformance, can trade weight for reps (e.g., 20kg x 10 -> 20kg x 11 ... 20kg x 15 -> 25kg x 6). No recommendation on first exercise use. Works with own plans and offline.
Effectively double progression driven by available increments: adds reps at the same load until the next weight step is appropriate (worked examples in docs), not a fixed rep-range rule.
Planned deload at end of a plan or mark any workout as deload; recommendations are reduced accordingly (Pro).
Intra-workout fatigue: recommendations change between sets because 'set 3 is not set 1'. No per-muscle recovery or readiness model - recovery handled by program structure.
No conversational/AI coach; algorithmic generators and recommendations only. Human support via email.
Free: weight, reps, volume, estimated 1RM, estimated 10RM records and best performance per muscle group, surfaced in workout summary.
Estimated 1RM and 10RM per set (setting chooses which metric is displayed). Internal 10RM uses AP's own method; public RM calculator combines Epley and Brzycki.
Pro charts: exercise performance, strength, volume, sets per muscle, workouts per week, bodyweight, measurements; configurable chart per exercise pinnable to Analytics; 3M range added 2026.
Sets-per-muscle and volume charts (Pro); reports break down by muscle.
No body heat map documented (older review mentions muscle targeting diagrams on exercises).

Weekly target 1-7 workouts; streak = consecutive weeks meeting target, plus view for all targets and consecutive days. Achievements with punny badges and trophies per 10%. Calendar-based weekly/monthly/yearly reports.
Post-workout summary lists all records beaten and comparison with previous workout; shareable screenshot.
Home page mentions a 'strength rating' chart; no population percentile/standards documented.
Weekly, monthly and yearly reports: frequency, what was trained, records, progress, achievements, most-used exercise, most-trained muscle, vs previous period.
Free; manual or from Apple Health/Health Connect; used for bodyweight-exercise load.
Free: bodyweight, body fat %, calves L/R, chest, forearms L/R, hips, neck, shoulder width, thighs L/R, upper arms L/R, waist; charts (absolute/change) in Pro.
Not documented.
No sleep/HRV/readiness inputs; the program-centric approach explicitly has no recovery model.
Apple Health (iOS) and Health Connect (Android): workouts with calories, bodyweight, body fat %. Health Connect data stays on device.
No Apple Watch or Wear OS app (on roadmap); Live Activity / live notification instead.
features.user_feedback: Most cited missing feature in reviews (fitnessdrum 2026; compareworkoutapps).

features.how: No Strava, Garmin or Fitbit integration stated by AP's own comparison.
No import from other apps; past workouts must be added manually.
Free CSV export of plans, workout history, custom exercises, body measurements; since v7.6.2 via email, direct .csv download or clipboard.
Optional free account syncs to backend across devices/iOS-Android incl. subscription; guest data local only and cannot be merged later.
No home-screen widget documented.
Not documented.
Pro: multiple gyms, each with own equipment and weights; without Pro only the active gym is usable.

Per gym, per equipment, per exercise: weight ranges (min/max/interval, multiple ranges) or bar weight + plate counts; per-equipment/per-exercise unit overrides. Defaults provided in kg and lb. Drives recommendations, warm-ups and plate calculator.
Equipment checklist (~40 items in 6 groups) filters database and generators; whitelist/blacklist exercises.
No built-in social network (AP's own comparison).
Screenshot of workout summary/report to social media or messenger; plan/workout links with QR code.
No social network or leaderboards.
Not documented (achievements exist).
No coach tooling; sharing plan links with coaching clients is the only mechanism.
Coach can send a plan link/QR; client gets an editable copy. No tracking of client.
No coach feedback; email support only.
Not available.
Not available.

Free forever, no ads, no account: unlimited logging, own plans, 795 exercise videos, rest timer, records, achievements, measurements, sharing, CSV. Pro $12.99/mo or $79.99/yr (US; 14-day trial only on yearly), via App Store, Play or web (web allows promo codes). Full refund on request. After expiry: generated-plan workouts can't be started; manual plans run without Pro settings.
features.user_feedback: Free users ask for periodization in free tier (App Store review).

features.how: kg/lb, cm/in, decimal point/comma, 12/24h, week start Sun/Mon; weight/length overridable per gym equipment and per exercise.
Light and dark mode.
13 languages (added most in Jul-Sep 2026: ES, FR, PT-BR, TR, IT, PL, NL, SV, NO, DA, JA; plus EN, DE).
App Store: developer has not indicated accessibility features.
Short onboarding: gender, experience (5 levels), bodyweight (manual or Health); optional Health connection; Pro offer; no account needed.
Almost fully offline incl. Pro recommendations; videos in lower resolution; generators need internet; sync when back online.
No account required (guest data local only). German GmbH, GDPR; uses Firebase, Adjust, RevenueCat/Stripe. App Store label: purchases and identifiers used to track; third-party advertising data.
iOS (iPhone, iOS 15.6+; listed for Vision), Android; no iPad-specific, watch, or web app.
